## ⚠️ First: the dispatch's hypothesis was wrong, and the dev is right about why

The claim comment offered a hypothesis for the 24-vs-23 discrepancy — "the likeliest reconciliation is that one occurrence is a code SAMPLE inside a string" — and marked it as a hypothesis rather than a reading. **It is false.** Verified here on `origin/main`: `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx:76` sits inside a `/** … */` **block comment** — #6580's own doc comment, which quotes the very `vi.mock('@object-ui/app-shell')` call it documents.

⭐ And the sharper half of the correction is the dev's: **the number quoted in the same dispatch already refuted the hypothesis.** The gate reports `3 embedded in a string literal` tree-wide, and none of those three names `@object-ui/app-shell` (two are `@object-ui/react` samples in the gate's own header, one is `./dep` in an eslint-rule test). Had the 24th been a string literal it would have appeared in that counter. The mechanism is different in kind: `scanSource()` blanks comments **before** `CALL_RE` runs, so a commented occurrence never becomes a call site and lands in **no** bucket at all. Measured: `comment[offset] = 1, literal[offset] = 0`.

⇒ No effect on scope — 23 was and is the right number, and 23 were converted. Only the explanation changes. ⭐ The reconciliation is now recorded in the gate's own header, which is the right home: it is a property of that file's masking behaviour, and it explicitly says that guessing `embedded` would have been wrong "in a way that reads plausible".

## The count, reconciled all three ways

| number | what it counts | why |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | distinct **files** — the card's own recipe | unreachable as a site count: `AppManagementPage.mutations.test.tsx` carries **two** sites (`vi.mock` at :89, `vi.doMock` at :280) |
| **23** | call **sites** per `scan()` | what this PR converted, one for one |
| 24 | `vi.mock`+`vi.doMock` **occurrences**, unmasked regex | the extra one is the block comment above |

## The census moved exactly as far as the diff, and no further

`625 judged / 625 inherit / 0 frozen; 35 other workspace` → **`648 / 648 / 0; 12 other workspace`**. Covered rose by 23, other-workspace fell by 23, and 648 + 12 = 660 both before and after ⇒ no site moved the other way and nothing joined the judged population except these. `@object-ui/app-shell` went 23 frozen → **0**. `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` is 19 and the header's count was updated with it.

## ⭐ The one site that could have gone wrong, and the reason it did not

`FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx` is the file **#6580 removed `importOriginal()` from**, because the barrel load cost **10204 ms of `hop1SessionPrincipal`'s 15000 ms budget**. This slice puts it back. That is the highest-risk edit in the PR and it is safe for a reason the file's own comment already contained: the module-scope `import { InternalFormRoute }` above is the first VALUE request for the specifier, so the factory — and the barrel load inside it — runs during the **IMPORT** phase, which no timeout bounds. #8173 measured it: `hop1SessionPrincipal` **9 ms → 8 ms**.

⭐ The dev appended eight lines to that comment rather than leaving it asserting the opposite of the code beside it, and declared the addition as its one non-factory edit. Nothing was removed from it. Checked in the diff: the factory now spreads `importOriginal()` **first**, with the pre-existing `vi.importActual` submodule spreads after it, so every current override still wins.

## Assertions

23 removed lines, every one a factory line — 15 plain multi-line `vi.mock`, 3 single-line, 2 async arrows returning an object literal, 2 with block bodies, 1 `vi.doMock`. The `vi.doMock` at `:280` is named in the PR body as the odd site, as the dispatch required: it runs inside a test after `vi.resetModules()`, so its obtain sits in a bounded window rather than the import phase — measured harmless at 459 → 660 ms against a 5000 ms budget.

## ⭐ The ablation near-miss is the most valuable line in the report

The first ablation used `perl -0pi -e`, **silently matched nothing, and exited 0** — leaving the file byte-identical to HEAD. It was caught only because the harness compares on-disk marker counts and blob hashes *before* reading any result, and it was **reported rather than quietly retried**. A green from an ablation that never mutated anything is the exact "clean number bought by not looking" failure this lane has now hit three times today in different disguises. The redone leg mutates by exact-string replacement with an asserted anchor count (marker 4 → 3, frozen-form 0 → 1, blob `673e5690…` → `cef53498…`), the gate then exits **1** naming `ApprovalsInboxPage.cellIdentity.test.tsx:123`, and the restore is proven by observation (`git diff HEAD` empty, hash back to `673e5690…`), not by an exit code.

Verification reproduces #8173's figures exactly — 22 files / 150 tests, and the console project at 89 files / 1069 tests — which is itself a cross-check between two independent runs a day apart. The changeset check was **run, not guessed**: it exited 1 first and demanded the declaration. One NOT-MEASURED datum is recorded rather than reported as a pass: `type-check` before the dependency build exits 2 with a wall of TS2307, which is the missing-dist class and not a red typecheck.

## ⭐ What this changes about the worklist, and it is more than one slice

The dev measured the tail rather than assuming it: **`@object-ui/plugin-view` reads 10 judged / 10 inheriting / 0 frozen, and `@object-ui/core` reads 2 / 2 / 0.** ⇒ Slices 15 and 16 are **pure membership flips of `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` with no test edits at all** — this slice was the last one carrying frozen sites, and the tree-wide figure across all 21 specifiers any `vi.mock` names is now **660 judged, 660 inherit, 0 frozen**. ⛔ Correctly not folded in: the dispatch forbade it and one-specifier-per-slice keeps a regression bisectable. But the card's remaining shape is now two cheap flips, not two sweeps, and that goes on the card at release.

Not governed surface (`--test` on all 24 paths ⇒ NOT GOVERNED). PR stays draft; the flip is this seat's read.
